title: Stochastic KV subpage allocator and multiplexed GPU-swap policy for low-latency continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Under mixed workloads with variable sequence lengths and continuous batching, the current slab-based KV cache suffers from subpage internal fragmentation and hotset thrashing when the GPU memory is oversubscribed. Eviction spikes cause tail-latency increases and intermittent OOM fallbacks for latency-sensitive requests. Goal: design and implement a paged/blocked KV cache variant that uses stochastic subpage allocation (subpage-sized granularity within pages) plus a multiplexed GPU-swap policy that enforces per-stream residency budgets and coordinated prefetch scoring. The design must preserve low token-level latency for streaming/interactive requests, reduce swap-induced stalls during large-batch throughput runs, and add lightweight telemetry to correlate swap events with batching patterns.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end implementation merged behind feature-flag: runtime.kv.subpage_alloc=true
Tail p99 token generation latency regression vs baseline <= 5% on interactive benchmarks (1-8 tokens) under 80% GPU occupancy
Overall token throughput for 512-token batch workload improves or is within 3% of baseline while reducing swap events by >= 30% under identical memory pressure
New telemetry published: kv.resident_ratio, kv.swap_events_per_min, kv.swap_stall_ms, kv.prefetch_score_histogram
Canary rollout plan documented with automatic rollback on >3% increase in error-rate or >10% increase in p99 latency
Comprehensive unit and stress tests including simulated OOM, multi-tenant sharing, and continuous-batching mix
design_decisions: Subpage allocator: pages remain 2MiB-aligned; page contains multiple fixed-size subpage slots (configurable powers of two: 4KiB, 16KiB, 64KiB) chosen by model shard hotness profile
Stochastic placement: on allocation, choose a candidate subpage lane using a weighted-random sampler biased toward lanes with lower fragmentation to avoid deterministic hot-spot packing
Multiplexed swap policy: keep per-request-stream soft residency budgets (tokens * avg_kv_size) and a global draining priority queue for swap-out candidates tagged with request-affinity and recency

Prefetch scoring: continuous-batcher signals predicted next-token keysets; score = alpha*access_frequency + beta*batch_affinity + gamma*kv_age - delta*swap_cost_estimate; tune coefficients in experiments
Hysteresis & grace windows: implement swap hysteresis (time and token-count) to avoid re-swapping items oscillating under alternating micro-batches
Backpressure integration: when resident_ratio < threshold, throttle large batching admission and opportunistically serve interactive streams from pinned hotset
Memory accounting: use host-side shadow accounting to maintain deterministic eviction choices without blocking main inference path; actual GPU copy performed asynchronously with priority lanes
Observability: emit aggregated per-model and per-pool metrics and sample traces for long-lived swap events to correlate with console dashboards
experiments: Microbench harness: synthetic mix (60% interactive small prompts, 40% throughput batches) with controlled GPU memory caps to measure swap events and latency impact
A/B on dedicated pool: deploy behind feature flag to 10% of requests on a single dedicated pool; compare swap event rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, and token throughput over 48h
Prefetch coefficient sweep: grid-search alpha/beta/gamma/delta on representative workloads to produce optimal coefficients for default config
Subpage size sensitivity: compare 4KiB/16KiB/64KiB subpage configs to find best trade-off between fragmentation and allocation overhead
Stress test: multi-tenant simulated bursts to validate hysteresis prevents thrash under adversarial arrival patterns
rollout_plan: Stage 0: implement behind flag + unit tests + integration tests in runtime repository
Stage 1: Canary on internal perf pool with synthetic traffic (48h). Roll forward if no regressions; otherwise iterate on heuristics
Stage 2: 10% traffic on low-risk dedicated pools (72h) with telemetry guardrails (auto rollback on latency/error thresholds)
Stage 3: 50% traffic and compare aggregated economics metrics (swap_bytes, swapped_tokens) vs baseline
Stage 4: Global rollout with opt-out knob per-customer and documentation of memory/config knobs and operational runbook
